questions.stem: Why is graphene an excellent electrical conductor?

options.text: It contains ionic bonds that allow ions to move
It contains metallic bonds between the carbon atoms
Each carbon bonds to only 3 others, leaving delocalised electrons that can carry charge
It is only one atom thick, so current can pass through easily

questions.explanation: In graphene, each carbon atom forms covalent bonds with only 3 other carbon atoms. The fourth outer electron from each carbon becomes delocalised and free to move across the sheet. These delocalised electrons can carry electrical charge, making graphene an excellent conductor - even better than copper.
